ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $\angle A = \angle B$, $AE = BE$, point $D$ is on side $AC$, $\angle 1 = \angle 2$, $AE$ and $BD$ intersect at point $O$, if $\angle 1 = 38^\circ$, then what is the degree measure of $\angle BDE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $AE$ and $BD$ intersect at point $O$,\\
$\therefore \angle AOD=\angle BOE$,\\
In $\triangle AOD$ and $\triangle BOE$, $\angle A=\angle B$,\\
$\therefore \angle BEO=\angle 2$,\\
$\because \angle 1=\angle 2$,\\
$\therefore \angle 1=\angle BEO$,\\
$\therefore \angle 1+\angle DEO=\angle BEO+\angle DEO$,\\
that is, $\angle AEC=\angle BED$,\\
In $\triangle AEC$ and $\triangle BED$,\\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}
\angle A=\angle B \\
\angle AEC=\angle BED \\
AE=BE
\end{array}\right.$\\
$\therefore \triangle AEC\cong\triangle BED\left(AAS\right)$,\\
$\therefore CE=DE$,\\
$\because \angle 1=38^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle C=\angle EDC=\frac{1}{2}\times \left(180^\circ-\angle 1\right)=\frac{1}{2}\times \left(180^\circ-38^\circ\right)=71^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle BDE=\boxed{71^\circ}$.
